verdict: The core wrap/proof/carry construction composes soundly: a byte-identical subset of a verified wrap set does open to the same M (each c_i - r_i*A_i = M holds independently), a carry cannot revive a kicked wrap (R4 copies only from head, C2 blocks replay), the sorted-first anchor A_1 carries no special status outside a single proof, and the signature scope covers what the transcript omits. The breaks are at the seams between the proof and the keyed world: (1) migration mints a genesis whose dek_gen contradicts C1/R2, so no migrated chain verifies and P6 filters every secret; (2) recovery as specified is refused by S2/S5 when it replaces authority/backup and the live server cannot serve during a per-group key swap; (3) recovery-with-rotate cannot be staged for the orphaned/hijacked groups it exists for (StageVersions is admin-gated); (4) the proof never binds M to dek_commit, S5 is scoped to rotating records, the DEK cache is keyed by the very field a liar copies, and S6 blocks the natural repair; (5) an authority carry-shrink is permitted in mode A, leaving a removed reader's retained wrap opening the live M with no write fence, regressing today's always-rotate revocation. Three minor findings: reencrypted digest defined over the installed set but computed over the staged set; retained old wraps plus no secure_delete/VACUUM make pre-rotation page residue readable by a kicked key; in-record duplicate c0 is not explicitly rejected, which is the one case where D1's related-key attack returns. The 'no key-committing AEAD needed' claim holds within the stated threat model; nonce handling and the KDF/commit separation are sound.

findings.title: Migration genesis has dek_gen = MAX(group_dek.version)+1 but every verifier requires genesis dek_gen = 1
findings.detail: 12.2: 'dek_gen = MAX(group_dek.version) + 1; re-encrypt every version under it; build genesis'. C1 and R2: genesis dek_gen = 1. Section 8 says group_dek.version 'continues the same counter, so secret_version.dek_version and crypto::secret_aad are untouched', and 3.4/10 make dek_version == dek_gen (the AAD field and the P6 filter secret.dek_version == head.dek_gen). Every existing group has group_dek v1, so MAX+1 >= 2. Either (a) the record carries MAX+1 and is rejected by C1/R2 at every replica (P2) and by `client epoch log`, so replicas serve their pre-migration mirror forever after the ALPN cut-over; or (b) the record carries 1 while rows carry MAX+1, and P6 filters every fetched secret so replicas converge on empty groups. The AAD/dek_gen composition the spec relies on is broken at the first record of every migrated chain.
findings.fix: State one rule everywhere: either relax C1/R2 to 'genesis: dek_gen >= 1 and equals the group_dek row inserted with it', or have migration delete retired group_dek rows first and insert the new generation as version 1 (PK (group_id, version) permits it in the same transaction) so rows carry dek_version = 1 and genesis dek_gen = 1; document that pre-migration snapshots then share AAD (group, name, version, 1) under a different DEK (harmless). Add to the 13 Store test: migrated genesis verifies AND its dek_gen equals every secret_version.dek_version.

findings.title: A recovery that replaces authority or backup is refused by S2 (and S5 in mode A), and the live server cannot serve during a per-group authority swap
findings.detail: 6.4 says this flow replaces `recover` ('one recovery per group replacing authority, with --rotate') with 'the service never stopped'. S2: 'The configured authority/backup ids equal the record's (also for genesis)'. A recovery with --authority <new> carries authority != configured and is Failed before C4's exemption matters. Even with S2 relaxed, mode A S5 requires the server to 'open its own wrap' in the submitted record; its wraps address the new authority (the old one is dropped, which is why G4/R6 force a rotate), so the server holding the old operational.key cannot run S5, cannot re-encrypt stragglers (S4), and cannot serve Get/Put afterwards (12.3: read_secret opens the head's authority wrap). Installing the new key first breaks reads for every not-yet-recovered group and S5's 'decrypt the row it replaces under the old DEK'. 'One recovery per group' implies a window needing both keys; meta.operational_ed25519 is a single value and nothing in 3.2/8/12 provides two. Same S2 mismatch refuses a recovery changing backup.
findings.fix: (1) S2: for kind = recovery compare authority/backup against the head (C4 already carries immutability), and require only that the record's new authority is the configured key or a configured next key. (2) Specify a two-key transition (`serve --operational-key new --previous-operational-key old` or meta.operational_ed25519_previous); read_secret/S5 choose whichever key is a recipient of the record in question; GroupStatus reports which groups still name the old authority. (3) State that for a recovery, S5 decrypts old rows with the head's authority wrap (old key) and encrypts stragglers under the new record's wrap. Add a server test: authority replacement across two groups one at a time with Get/Put working throughout.

findings.section: 6.4 step 3 vs 9 table (StageVersions requires admin) and 5 R6/G4
findings.title: Recovery-with-rotate cannot be staged for the groups recovery exists for: StageVersions is admin-gated and an orphaned or hijacked group has no usable admin
findings.detail: 6.4 triggers: rogue admin lock-out, all admin keys lost, operational-key compromise, authority/backup replacement, mode change. Every one except 'add an admin back' is forced to be a rotate by R6/G4 (removing the rogue admin, old authority, old backup, or the server on A->E removes a recipient), and a rotate needs its re-encrypted set delivered through StageVersions ('staged like 6.1'). The 9 table gates StageVersions on `admin`. In the all-keys-lost and RemoveIdentity-orphaned cases there is no admin; in the rogue-admin case the only admin is the one being removed. 'any registered identity: client epoch submit --bundle g.recovery (S1 exception)' can deliver the record but not the stage, so SubmitEpoch fails S4 coverage. S1's exception was written for the record and forgotten for the stage; 'one open stage per (group, submitter)' and the epoch_stage schema have no notion of a recovery stage.
findings.fix: Extend the S1 exception to StageVersions for recovery: accept a stage from any registered identity when accompanied by (or followed within the TTL by) a recovery record whose author is head.backup (e.g. `StageVersions{..., recovery_hash}` admitted only for a verified-but-uninstalled A4 record), or simply admit stages from any registered identity under the existing per-group byte cap and TTL, since a stage touches nothing until a verified record claims it. Add the 13 e2e case (7) with --rotate.

findings.section: 5 S5 scope, S8/7.1 DEK cache key, 7.4 last row, 3.8, 5 S6
findings.title: The proof never binds M to dek_commit; S5 (the only keyed check) is scoped to rotating records, the DEK cache is keyed by the copied commit, and the '(R1 + R3) checked at submit by a party with no key' claim is false
findings.detail: 3.8 correctly says nothing is claimed about M. So an admin (or buggy client) can build a rewrap for a fresh M' != M with a valid proof and copy head.dek_commit. Every keyless rule passes: R2 (commit == head's), R3 (dek_commit is an opaque transcript string, not a relation to M'), R5, C3, A2, G*. Only 3.6 step 5 by a recipient detects it. S5 is introduced as 'opens its own wrap, checks dek_commit, decrypts every staged row...', invoked only in the 6.1 rotate commit sequence; 6.2 (rewrap) never mentions it. As written the garbage rewrap is installed as head. S8/7.1 then cache the DEK per (group_id, dek_commit): the new head has the old commit, so every Get/Put on the authoritative node hits the cache and keeps working, while every replica (P4) and reader fails closed and the backup key's head wrap opens to garbage, exactly the 'invisible until disaster day' property 7.5 says the proof prevents. 7.4's last row ('Impossible (R1 + R3), checked at submit by a party with no key') and 7.1's 'submit-time guarantee that the backup key's wrap opens' hold only with a keyed check; mode E has none. Repair is blocked: an honest rewrap re-issuing correct wraps for the same ACL is refused by S6 as a no-op, forcing a full rotate or recovery.
findings.fix: (1) S5's first clause applies to every proof-bearing kind (genesis, rewrap, rotate, recovery): in mode A the server MUST open its own wrap and check dek_commit before S3; staged-row clauses stay rotate-only. (2) Key the DEK cache by record hash (or (group_id, dek_commit, hash)), or populate it only from a wrap the server actually opened for that record. (3) Reword 7.4/7.1: keyless verification guarantees equality across recipients; equality with the committed key is guaranteed at submit only by the mode-A server's own wrap, and in mode E only at first use. (4) S6: exempt a rewrap whose head fails the submitter's commit check (or a `repair` reason). (5) Negative server test: rewrap with copied commit and wrong M is refused by S5 and nothing is cached.

findings.section: 5 R6 / A3 vs 6.3 legacy Grant, 7.4 rows 'Compromised reader key' and 'Stolen SQLite (authoritative)', D6
findings.title: An authority carry that drops a reader is permitted in mode A: the removed reader's retained wrap opens the live M, no write fence exists, and today's always-rotate revocation regresses
findings.detail: R6 allows 'carry with author = authority (flags needs_rotation)' with no mode restriction; A3 allows authority carry in either mode. 6.3 routes RemoveIdentity in mode A to rotate, but routes legacy Grant shrinks to 'carry/rotate per A3' without saying which when read is cleared, and the only Put fence for needs_rotation is stated under the mode-E branch. Today (crypto-design.md 4 wrap lifecycle; store.rs revoke_read_and_rotate; main.rs db_grant) losing read always rotates. Valid mode-A chain under the new rules: #10 rotate gen 9 by alice, wraps {A,B,srv,bk}; #11 authority carry after Grant{bob, perms: w} dropping B, needs_rotation = 1; no admin rotates for days. B's wrap in #10 is retained forever and opens M_9, still the live generation: a stolen SQLite plus B's key reads every retained version and everything written after the 'kick' until someone rotates, contradicting 7.4 'old records' wraps open an M that protects nothing' and 'after the rotate nothing in the database is under a generation it knew'; mode A keeps accepting plaintext Put under M_9 with no fence, losing 'Future writes are protected'; nothing forces the rotate. The carry-shrink shape exists for mode E where the server cannot rotate; in mode A the authority can (A3) and RemoveIdentity already does.
findings.fix: R6: 'or kind = carry with author = authority, permitted only when mode = E'. A3: in mode A any authority record removing a read recipient MUST be a rotate. 6.3 legacy Grant: 'read cleared -> rotate (mode A) as today; w/a-only -> carry'. If needs_rotation survives in mode A (e.g. after a recovery-authored carry), state the mode-A Put behaviour and caveat 7.4's two rows with 'while needs_rotation is clear'. Add test: legacy Grant clearing read in mode A produces a rotate, never a carry.

findings.title: reencrypted is defined as the digest of the installed set but S4 computes it over the staged set as submitted, so after stragglers or interleaved deletes no verifier can recompute it and the attribution line names the admin for ciphertext the server produced
findings.detail: 4.3: 'Over the ciphertext set installed with a rotating record'. S4: digest 'computed by the server over the staged set as submitted. Rows staged for a version deleted meanwhile are ignored. In mode A ... stragglers are re-encrypted by the server itself at commit'. The signed digest thus includes leaves never installed (deleted meanwhile) and excludes straggler rows whose nonces/ciphertexts the admin never saw. An offline auditor recomputing 4.3 from group_epoch/secret_version gets a different value from every rotation that raced a writer and cannot distinguish that from tampering. 6.5 prints 'alice rotate gen 9 re-encrypted 143 versions' under alice's signature over a set that is partly not what is stored; the server's share exists only in the unsigned audit row. Not a confidentiality break in mode A, but a spec-internal contradiction that weakens the one keyless attribution claim the field exists for.
findings.fix: Either define reencrypted honestly as 'digest of the set the author submitted; the installed set may differ by server-re-encrypted stragglers and versions deleted meanwhile, recorded in the audit row' and drop 'installed' from 4.3; or make mode A two-phase like mode E: answer StaleVersions with the straggler list and have the client re-stage and re-sign, bounding loops with the stage TTL and the short write fence 7.2 already plans.

findings.section: 3.8 forward secrecy, 7.4 'Stolen SQLite (authoritative)', D6, 8 (group_epoch retains every record)
findings.title: Old records deliberately retain every recipient's wrap of retired M, but nothing scrubs the retired ciphertext from the SQLite file, so a kicked reader's key still reads the pre-rotation pages of a stolen file
findings.detail: Versus today, retired wraps are no longer deleted (store.rs revoke_read_and_rotate deletes dek_wrap rows for the revoked recipient) but kept in group_epoch, justified by 'old records' wraps open an M that protects nothing'. That is true of live rows only. Rotation is `UPDATE secret_version SET dek_version, nonce, ciphertext` on a database opened with journal_mode = WAL and no secure_delete (store.rs 239-250; no secure_delete or VACUUM anywhere). Previous page images persist in the WAL until checkpoint and in freelist pages until reused. Sequence: bob is kicked at #12 (gen 9 -> 10); the file is stolen a week later; bob's key opens his wrap in #11 (retained), derives DEK_9, and decrypts every pre-rotation version still in free pages, with AAD (group, name, version, 9) reconstructible from live rows. Today the residue exists but bob's gen-9 wrap is deleted, so it is opaque to him. Migration rewrites every ciphertext once and leaves the whole pre-migration database in free pages.
findings.fix: Set PRAGMA secure_delete = ON for authoritative and replica databases, VACUUM at the end of db migrate-epochs, and PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) after every rotation commit. Caveat 7.4 ('protects nothing in the live rows; free-page residue is scrubbed by secure_delete'). Alternatively retain only the head's wraps plus hash-chained bodies of older records, dropping retired wraps as today.

findings.section: 5 R5 / E2 wording vs D1 rationale and 3.3
findings.title: R5 rejects c0 reuse against earlier records only; duplicate c0 inside one record is not rejected, which is the one case where D1's related-key attack comes back
findings.detail: 3.3 says c0_i values are 'unique across the whole chain (verifier rule R5)', but R5 reads 'no c0_i equals any c0 seen earlier in the chain' and E2 requires strict ascending order for ids, not c0. A record with c0_i == c0_j (r_i == r_j) passes E2, R3 (the proof is valid for any r vector) and R5 as written. D1's 'closes it by construction' assumes independent r_i; if the same r reaches recipients A and -A (an id registrable by flipping the sign bit of A's hex, D1's own example) then c_A + c_{-A} = 2M and M is public from the record. The realistic path is the RNG failure the hedged nonce exists to survive: a forked VM or snapshot-restored admin client repeating OsRng output yields r_i == r_j with no proof failure, and R5 catches it only across records. The check is one set insert per wrap and the seen-c0 set already exists.
findings.fix: E2: 'acl and wraps are strictly ascending by id; all c0_i within the record are pairwise distinct'. R5: 'no c0_i equals any c0 in this record or seen earlier in the chain'. Add 'two wraps with equal c0' to the 13 negative matrix and a property test that related-key recipients with duplicated r_i are rejected before the M-recovery formula is reachable.
